sections.name: File setup, FactRow, Paged
sections.title: Purpose and the basic row types
sections.what: Explains what this file is for and defines two small shapes: a fact row for evidence shown in slide tables, and a page counter used by long slides.
sections.why: The header says the deck follows a reference structure, that everything paginates, and that evidence gaps are stated on the slide that would hold them.
sections.watch_out: The slide order is said to follow a reference document, so changing the order means checking that document too.

sections.name: DeckSlide, OUTCOMES, fmtM, or
sections.title: Slide types and formatting helpers
sections.what: Defines every kind of slide the deck can hold and the fields each one needs. Also defines the four outcome labels and two helpers: one formats money in millions or billions and shows Not recorded when blank, and one puts a placeholder into empty text.
sections.why: Likely reason: one list of slide kinds lets the viewer and the PowerPoint renderer agree on what each slide contains.
sections.watch_out: Money is shown in millions and switches to billions at 1000, so a wrong unit in a stored budget shows directly as a wrong figure.

sections.name: paginate
sections.title: Splitting rows into pages
sections.what: Splits a list into pages so each page stays under a rough size limit. Long lists become several slides instead of being cut off.
sections.why: This is how long tables stay complete across slides, as the file header requires.
sections.watch_out: The size is a character count, not a real layout measurement, so a page can still overflow on the slide.

sections.name: extractAbbreviations
sections.title: Finding abbreviations and their full names
sections.what: Scans fact and methodology text for a full name followed by a short form in brackets, and keeps the pair when the short form matches the first letters of the name. The result feeds the abbreviations appendix.
sections.why: Likely reason: readers of a long deck need a glossary, and building it from the text avoids keeping a fixed list.
sections.watch_out: Only the first full name found for each short form is kept, so a short form used for two different things shows one meaning.

sections.name: buildDeck (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up the deck and dropping empty pillars
sections.what: Starts the slide list. It removes any pillar with no admitted fact and no finding, records that it was pruned and why, and adds the opening slides and one set of pillar pages for each remaining pillar.
sections.why: Likely reason: a pillar with no evidence should be stated as pruned rather than shown as an empty driver, as the code comment says.
sections.watch_out: A pillar is removed when both its fact count and finding count are zero, so a wrong count in the assessment removes a real pillar.

sections.name: buildDeck: for
sections.title: Adding sub-driver, rubric and matrix slides
sections.what: For each sub-driver, adds pages of good examples and cautionary tales, with a gap note when no admitted fact supports it. Then adds the rubric, the study universe, the project matrix, the cross-case synthesis, the two glossary slides and the cost versus schedule chart.
sections.why: Likely reason: each slide shows the data behind a claim, and the gap notes keep weak evidence visible.
sections.watch_out: The rubric note describes how cell scores are formed, so changing the scoring rule means changing that text too.

sections.name: buildDeck: for
sections.title: Adding case, factbase, programme and learning slides
sections.what: For each assessed project, adds a case summary and one or more factbase pages listing supporting facts grouped by pillar. A very short last page is merged into the one before it. Then adds the country comparison and the slide on how projects captured lessons.
sections.why: Likely reason: merging a near-empty last page avoids a slide with almost nothing on it. The three-project minimum for countries is not explained in the code.
sections.watch_out: The country comparison leaves out any country with fewer than three assessed projects, so a project can be missing from it without a note.

sections.name: buildDeck (part 4)
sections.title: Adding methodology, verification and closing slides
sections.what: Adds the methodology and source pages, the verification page with counts of verified, partial, unreachable and held facts, the abbreviation pages, and a closing slide saying every statement traces to a fact, finding or source.
sections.why: Likely reason: readers need to see how many facts were checked and held back, so the deck does not hide its own filtering.
sections.watch_out: The closing slide makes a traceability promise, so any statement added without a citation would make that promise false.

summary: Builds the ordered list of slide descriptions for the Lessons Learnt deck, which both the in-app viewer and the PowerPoint export read.
purpose: Turn the analysed results (framework, cases, facts, methodology) into one fixed, paged list of slides, so the screen and the PowerPoint file show the same content.
why: Likely reason: one shared slide list keeps the viewer and the PowerPoint file consistent. The header says the structure follows a reference document kept in the docs folder; the reason for each slide's place in the order is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Drop pillars with no evidence and record that they were pruned. 2. Add the opening slides: cover, executive summary, agenda and the framework overview. 3. Add pillar pages and sub-driver pages, splitting long lists by size. 4. Add the rubric, study universe, project matrix and cross-case synthesis. 5. Add the two glossary slides and the cost versus schedule chart. 6. Add a case summary and factbase pages for each assessed project. 7. Add the country comparison and the lessons-capture slide. 8. Add methodology, verification, abbreviation and closing slides.
inputs: A title, an industry label, the framework, assessment, methodology and synthesis, plus the project, fact, finding and commentary lists.
outputs: An ordered array of slide descriptions. Each has an id, a section name and a kind that tells the renderer which layout to use.
risks: Page sizes are character estimates, so text can overflow a real slide. Pillars are removed based on assessment counts, so a wrong count removes a real pillar from the deck. The closing slide promises that every statement is traceable, which only holds if every statement is cited.
debug: If a slide is missing, check whether the data array feeding it is empty, since many slides are skipped quietly when there is no data. If text overflows, lower the budget numbers passed to paginate. If a pillar is missing, check its fact and finding counts in the assessment.
